title: Bilateral grip-change discordance did not improve elevated-HbA1c prediction in a separate NHANES release
abstract: In adults with complete maximal-effort bilateral grip measurements, adding discordance of hand-specific first-to-third fractional grip change to age, sex, race/ethnicity, BMI, maximal grip, body-mass-normalized grip and maximal-grip asymmetry did not improve the locked model's prediction of concurrent HbA1c≥6.5%. Training used NHANES2011–2012(n=4073); confirmation used separately sampled2013–2014(n=4491). Weighted Brier gain was -0.00015587 (source-and-target PSU-refit95% interval -0.00113481 to 0.00029814;positive favors augmentation). This is a scoped negative prediction result,not evidence of absent physiological information or a validated diabetes screening test.
